text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi reaffirmed the need to extend talks on welfare state reforms to the majority of political allies, while hard left Communist Refoundation president Armando Cossutta repeated his party strongly opposed cuts to pensions (all).
* The Italian cabinet held a meeting in order to speed up the presentation of the DPEF, the government's three-year economic programme which should soon be ready (all).

* Fiat honorary chairman Giovanni Agnelli said Italy should make every possible effort in order to join the first wave of EMU. Agnelli also said welfare state should not be abolished but modernised (all).
* Electricity group Enel said its net profit rose 10.9 percent to 1.272 trillion lire in 1996 compared to 1.147 trillion in 1995 (all).

* European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said the commission was worried about the debt of state industrial holding IRI. Italian government designed a plan to reduce the group's debt but the operation is not yet finished (all).
* Latest Bank of Italy figures showed bad loans in the Italian banking system rose 0.68 percent to 115.444 trillion lire in February from 114.657 trillion in January (Sole 24 Ore).
* A study by research institute Isco showed Italian families in May were less pessimistic than in April about their economic prospects but were still worried about unemployment (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
